stl.invalidFile: Invalid file. Please upload STL, OBJ or 3MF.
stl.printTimeProfitHint: Time used in the profit-per-hour calculation

stl.estimationModeCustomDescription: Fine-tuning: per-material k factor + real G-code as anchor.
stl.estimationModeHelp: Standard: instant estimate from profile parameters (±30%). Custom: fine-tuning with per-material k factor + real G-code as anchor.
stl.calibrationKFormula: Final weight and time × k — e.g.: 10 g × 1.2 = 12 g
stl.advancedUncertainty: Pre-slice estimate (±30%). Slicer G-code is more accurate.
stl.gcodeEPathsNote: G-code E paths can differ: file view uses max-E, the Custom anchor sums extrusion (M82/M83 + G92). Retraction-heavy or relative files may diverge.
stl.assumptionsTooltip: The parameters that fed this estimate. Edit them in the Complete (advanced) mode — slicing profile and filament parameters.
stl.assumptionsRoughTooltip: Pre-slice approximation: only your slicer knows the real retractions, acceleration and supports. That's why this mode is conservative (errs on the high side).
stl.assumptionsWhyTitle: Why doesn't it match my slicer?
stl.assumptionsWhyText: This is a pre-slice estimate (±30%): it can't see retractions, travel, acceleration or supports. To match your slicer, use Custom mode with the real G-code as an anchor — it replaces weight and time with exact values.

welcome.title: Welcome to Open3DCalc!
welcome.description: Let's calculate the cost of your 3D prints together. Start by filling in the material data — we've already added example values for you to test.

material.title: Materials
material.description: Here you define the filament type, part weight, and cost. We've set PLA at $90/kg as an example — adjust according to your actual values.

print.title: Print Parameters
print.description: Enter the print time, your printer's power, and the energy cost. These values are essential for an accurate calculation.

sales.title: Pricing
sales.description: Now let's set your profit margin. Here you can also add packaging and shipping costs.

results.title: Results
results.description: Done! Here's the total cost, suggested price, and estimated profit. Use the sliders to simulate different scenarios.

export.title: Export
export.description: Save your calculation to history or export as PDF to send to your client.

complete.title: All set!
complete.description: Now you know how to calculate the cost of any print. Use the tooltips on each field if you have questions. Happy printing!

upload-intro.title: Bring in your 3D file
upload-intro.description: This tour shows how to import an STL, OBJ, 3MF, or G-code and explore the built-in 3D viewer.

upload-dropzone.title: Drop your file here
upload-dropzone.description: Drag a file onto this zone or click to browse your computer. Files are capped at 100 MB.

upload-samples.title: Sample models
upload-samples.description: No file of your own? Load the 3DBenchy STL to inspect the mesh, or its G-code to preview the toolpath.

upload-viewport.title: 3D viewer
upload-viewport.description: Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, and use the toolbar buttons to refit the frame or go fullscreen.

upload-complete.title: Ready to calculate
upload-complete.description: With a model loaded, the volume and weight estimates feed the calculator automatically. See the calculator tour for the details.

inv-intro.title: Manage your filament
inv-intro.description: This tour shows how to register a spool, use search and material filters, and read the stock card grid.

inv-add.title: Add a spool
inv-add.description: This button opens the form to register weight, material, color, and price for a new spool.

inv-search.title: Find it fast
inv-search.description: Type to search by name, material, or color — the grid filters as you type.

inv-filters.title: Filter by material
inv-filters.description: These buttons narrow the stock to a specific material in one click.

inv-grid.title: Your stock cards
inv-grid.description: Each card shows remaining weight, the consumption bar, and the low-stock alert.

inv-complete.title: Stock under control
inv-complete.description: The inventory feeds weight and price into the calculator. Check the dashboard tour to track your KPIs.

dash-intro.title: Your numbers in one place
dash-intro.description: This tour shows the financial summary, the date-range filter, the history KPIs, and the monthly profit projection.

dash-summary.title: Quick summary
dash-summary.description: Total cost, sale price, profit, and ROI for the filtered period — updated on every calculation.

dash-date-range.title: Filter the period
dash-date-range.description: Set a start and end date to narrow the analysis. Clear the filters anytime to see everything again.

dash-kpis.title: History KPIs
dash-kpis.description: Total profit, average cost per print, average margin, and print count for the selected period.

dash-projection.title: Monthly projection
dash-projection.description: Enter how many parts you print per month to estimate projected profit and plan your prices.

dash-complete.title: Data-driven decisions
dash-complete.description: Tweak the period and monthly volume to simulate scenarios. History keeps every calculation for later comparison.

qc-intro.title: Quotes and customers
qc-intro.description: In this tour you turn saved calculations into professional quotes and keep your clients organized in one place.

qc-list.title: Quotes list
qc-list.description: Every quote lives here, with status (draft, sent, approved or rejected) plus search by title or client.

qc-new.title: New quote
qc-new.description: Use this button to create a new quote from the calculations saved in your history.

qc-customer.title: Link a customer
qc-customer.description: In the form, pick the customer in the selector to link them to the quote — the contact is printed on the PDF.

cs-intro.title: Customers
cs-intro.description: Now the Customers tab: register name, company and contacts to reuse across quotes.

cs-list.title: Customers list
cs-list.description: Your client roster shows up here, with search plus actions to edit and remove entries.

cs-new.title: New customer
cs-new.description: Register a new customer with name, company, email, phone and notes.

qc-complete.title: Ready to quote!
qc-complete.description: Customer registered and quote linked: export it as a PDF and send it. Everything stays saved on your device.

adv-intro.title: Complete mode
adv-intro.description: This tour switches the calculator to the advanced level and walks the sections that add up every cost factor of a print.

adv-level.title: Switch the level
adv-level.description: The level selector controls how many sections the calculator shows. Advanced unlocks all ten — let's turn it on now.

adv-failure.title: Failure rate
adv-failure.description: Set the most common failure mode and the value of the lost part. The risk becomes a multiplier that weighs on every print.

adv-hardware.title: Hardware & post-processing
adv-hardware.description: Add the cost of replacement parts and finishing (sanding, gluing, assembly) that consume material and time.

adv-machine.title: Machine cost
adv-machine.description: Set the printer price, its expected lifespan and working hours to amortize the investment per print.

adv-fixedCost.title: Fixed costs
adv-fixedCost.description: Power, rent, internet and subscriptions: enter your monthly fixed costs and the calculator splits them across your output.

adv-labor.title: Labor
adv-labor.description: Set your hourly rate and the prep and finishing time each part takes.

adv-ops.title: Software & consumables
adv-ops.description: Slicer, modeling software, consumables and ongoing maintenance — the day-to-day operating costs.

adv-results.title: Complete result
adv-results.description: With every factor filled in, the result shows the full cost breakdown and the suggested sale price at the advanced level.

adv-complete.title: Cost mastered
adv-complete.description: You've added material, machine, labor, fixed costs and failures. Tweak any section and the result recalculates instantly.

slide1.title: What is Open3DCalc?
slide1.description: A free and open-source calculator to accurately estimate 3D printing costs.

slide2.title: How to calculate
slide2.description: Fill in material data, print parameters, and additional costs. Results are calculated automatically.

slide3.title: Save and track
slide3.description: Save your calculations to history, compare results, and export quotes as PDF.

banner.text: Your data stays only in your browser. Nothing you type — customer data, quotes, or logs — is sent to servers. You have full control: export, import, or delete your data anytime.

consent.title: Your Data Privacy
consent.text1: By using Open3DCalc's customer and quote features, you acknowledge that:
consent.item1: All data is stored exclusively in your browser's localStorage.
consent.item2: No data is transmitted, copied, or stored on external servers.
consent.item3: You are solely responsible for data backup and security.
consent.item4: Data may be lost when clearing browser cache — we recommend periodic backups.
consent.item5: This software does not collect telemetry, analytics, or personal information.
consent.accept: I understand and want to continue

policy.title: Privacy Policy
policy.section8Intro: Open3DCalc supports local data export and import via encrypted .open3dcalc bundles:
policy.section8Item2: All data processing happens exclusively client-side
policy.section8Item3: No data is transmitted to any server during export or import
policy.section8Item4: You can encrypt bundles with your own password
policy.section8Lgpd: In compliance with LGPD Art. 18 (right to data portability), you can export your data at any time and import it on another device.

quarantine.title: Legacy data quarantine
quarantine.subtitle: Personal data written in plaintext by older versions is quarantined: readable, but blocked from new writes until you choose to migrate (encrypt) or eliminate it.
quarantine.desktopOnly: Legacy data quarantine is available only in the desktop app, where data is durable in SQLite. On the web, your data stays local to the browser.
quarantine.noQuarantined: No data in quarantine. Everything stored is already encrypted or is not personal data.
quarantine.confirmMigrate: Migrate "{{key}}" to encryption at rest? The plaintext copy is only destroyed after the encrypted copy is verified.
quarantine.confirmEliminate: Permanently eliminate the quarantined data of "{{key}}"? This action cannot be undone.
quarantine.migrateFailed: Failed to migrate "{{key}}" — nothing was lost; please try again.
quarantine.eliminateFailed: Failed to eliminate "{{key}}" — the data stays quarantined.
quarantine.readNote: Quarantine never resolves on its own: the only exits are migrate or eliminate, always through your explicit action.
quarantine.loadError: Could not load the quarantine report.

erasure.title: Delete all my data
erasure.description: Removes all your data from every app storage surface (database, files, caches and internal backups), verifiably and with a receipt. Export packages you saved outside the app are out of reach.
erasure.working: Erasing… this may take a moment.
erasure.done: Erasure completed and verified. All stores have been wiped.
erasure.externalCopies: External copies the app cannot erase:
erasure.confirm: Delete ALL your data? An encrypted snapshot allows rollback for up to 7 days in case of failure. Once committed, removal is permanent. Continue?
erasure.failed: Erasure failed — your data was restored from the safety snapshot (when available) and nothing was lost.

consent_receipt.title: Consent
consent_receipt.granted: Consent active for policy v{{version}} (verified receipt).
consent_receipt.absent: No valid consent recorded — consent-gated features stay blocked.
consent_receipt.withdrawConfirm: Withdraw consent? Data collected under it will be erased per policy (SPEC-04 §6) and the affected features will be blocked.
consent_receipt.flagsNote: Tutorial, onboarding or banner flags never substitute consent — only the receipt counts (SPEC-04 §2).

tooltip.costPerKg: Average price per kg of filament. PLA ~R$90, PETG ~R$110, ABS ~R$100.
tooltip.purge: Weight wasted in purge tower or color change. Can be larger than the part in multicolor prints!
tooltip.spoolEfficiency: You never use 100% of a spool. End-of-spool leftovers and changes reduce efficiency. Default: 95-98%.
tooltip.wasteMargin: Resin lost in VAT, extra supports, cleaning. Suggested: 5-10%.
tooltip.risk: Increases risk for complex geometries or long prints. 1.0 = Normal, 1.5 = High risk.
tooltip.nozzleCost: Brass is cheap, Hardened Steel is expensive. Wear depends on material (abrasives wear fast).
tooltip.nozzleLife: How many kg of filament does this nozzle last? Brass w/ PLA: ~20kg. Steel w/ CF: ~10kg.
tooltip.bedCost: Estimated cost of spray, glue or PEI sheet wear per print.
tooltip.finishing: Estimated cost of sandpaper, primer, paints, putty or acetone used on this part.
tooltip.ppe: Gloves, masks, paper towels, filters, etc. Fixed cost per print.
tooltip.marketplaceFee: Percentage charged by the marketplace on the sale value.
tooltip.printTimeHours: Total time the print takes to complete. Use the value from your slicer software.
tooltip.printerPowerWatts: Average power consumption of your printer. Most FDM printers use between 100W and 350W.
tooltip.energyCostPerKwh: Your electricity rate per kWh. Check your utility bill for the exact value.
tooltip.machineCost: How much you paid for the printer. Include shipping and taxes if possible.
tooltip.depreciationMonths: Over how many months the printer will be paid off. 36 months is standard for equipment.
tooltip.hoursPerMonth: How many hours per month the printer is running.
tooltip.maintenanceCost: Estimated monthly maintenance cost (nozzles, belts, lubrication).
tooltip.setupTime: Time spent preparing the file, slicing, and setting up the printer.
tooltip.postProcessingTime: Time removing the part from the bed, removing supports, sanding.
tooltip.hourlyRate: How much you want to earn per hour of work. Your time is valuable.
tooltip.quantity: How many identical units will be produced. Setup cost is diluted across units.
tooltip.infillPercent: How much of the interior will be filled. 15% for decorative, 50%+ for functional parts.
tooltip.shipping: Shipping cost for delivery to the customer.
tooltip.taxPercent: Taxes on the sale value (varies by country and region).
tooltip.profitMargin: Markup: profit over cost. Margin: profit over the price the customer pays.
tooltip.infillDimension: Part dimension in centimeters to estimate volume.
tooltip.wallThickness: Thickness of the outer walls of the part.
tooltip.layerHeight: Height of each layer. 0.08mm = high quality, 0.28mm = economical.
tooltip.infillDensity: Internal fill percentage. 15% for decorative, 50%+ for functional.
tooltip.topBottomLayers: Number of solid layers on top and bottom of the part.
tooltip.alcoholCostPerLiter: Price per liter of isopropyl alcohol for washing. ~$5-12/L. Reuse filtered to save.
tooltip.washType: Water-washable resins are cleaned under running water (no alcohol). The medium is reset automatically when switching resins, but you are free to adjust it manually here.
tooltip.alcoholVolume: How many liters of alcohol are consumed per washing cycle. ~0.1-0.3L per batch of parts.
tooltip.cureTime: UV curing time after washing the part.
tooltip.curePower: Power of the UV lamp in the curing station.
tooltip.lcdCost: Cost of the LCD screen replacement for your resin printer.
tooltip.lcdLife: Estimated lifespan of the LCD screen in hours before replacement.
tooltip.fepCost: Cost of FEP film replacement for the resin vat.
tooltip.fepLife: Number of prints the FEP film lasts before needing replacement.
tooltip.slicerCost: Monthly cost of slicing software, if applicable.
tooltip.modelCost: Cost of the 3D file if you purchased the model from a third party.
tooltip.failureValue: Expected failure rate. 10% is a good starting default.
tooltip.costPerLiter: Average price per liter of resin. Standard ~$30-50/L.
tooltip.volumeMl: Volume of resin used in the part in milliliters.
tooltip.weightUsed: Weight of the part in grams. Use the value from your slicer.
tooltip.filamentType: Type of filament. PLA for beginners, PETG for strength, ABS for high temperature.
tooltip.slicerProfile: Your slicer's actual parameters. They feed the weight and time estimate of the 3D file — the closer they match your slicer, the more accurate the estimate (±30% envelope).
tooltip.slicerWallCount: Number of outer perimeters (walls). 2 is standard; 3+ for functional parts. 0 = vase mode (shell only, no solid wall).
tooltip.slicerLineWidth: Extruded line width in mm. Usually matches the nozzle diameter (0.4 nozzle → 0.42 mm).
tooltip.slicerTopLayers: Solid layers on top of the part. 4 layers at 0.2 mm ≈ 0.8 mm top.
tooltip.slicerBottomLayers: Solid layers at the base of the part. 4 layers at 0.2 mm ≈ 0.8 mm base.
tooltip.slicerLayerHeight: Height of each layer in mm. 0.08 = high quality, 0.2 = standard, 0.28 = economical.
tooltip.slicerPrintSpeed: Average print speed in mm/s. Higher speeds shorten the time but require more hotend volumetric flow.
tooltip.filamentProfile: Physical filament parameters that feed the weight and time estimate. These are local preferences only — no data is collected or synced.
tooltip.filamentPurgePercent: Purge/wipe percentage added on top of the extruded weight (AMS color changes, wipe tower into infill). Default 10%; 0 disables purge.
tooltip.filamentDiameter: Filament diameter in mm. 1.75 is the de facto standard; ±0.05 mm tolerances already shift volume by ~5.7%.
tooltip.filamentMvs: Maximum volumetric flow (mm³/s) the hotend delivers. Empty = material table (conservative). High-flow hotends (volcano/CHT) double the real MVS — fill it in if yours is fast.
